rows.model_basis: storage_power_mw - 1,865.0 MW PS residual (battery-only, per the D29 classification note)
rows.anchor_basis: AEO Diurnal Storage (batteries only; AEO books PS separately)
rows.explanation: Zero storage entry through 2049 UNDER THE ARMED POSTURE (run_config: storage_entry_availability_gate=true, storage_entry_cost_normalized_rank=true — owner ruling R-A), so the battery fleet at this anchor is still the 0.77 GW EIA-860 base and the -56.2 % divergence is UNCHANGED by the arming — itself a measured campaign result (T3-GOLDEN-2 finding §6). RE-AUTHORED per D36 §7 to name the driver, which the prior wording ('the value stack clears no tech') did not. THE DRIVER — PROCUREMENT CHANNEL UNREPRESENTED, the same instrument family as the offshore-wind rows (D25 §4.3 mechanism 3): AEO2025 carries New England's storage procurement obligations as policy inputs (the Massachusetts 2024 climate statute's 5,000 MW storage directive by 2030, Connecticut Public Act 21-53's 1,000 MW storage target, the MA Clean Peak Energy Standard credit stream — each an enforceable public instrument to be confirmed at intake, and each formulaic in the rule-13 sense: a dated MW obligation, not a fitted quantity); the model builds storage only through the merchant economic screen, so a contracted MW obligation has no way in. Were that channel ever chartered it would enter as a known-additions row (step 4), never through the screen. THE MODEL-SIDE RESIDUAL (R-1) — the merchant stack's own arbitrage blindness: D36 reconstructs the value stack year by year and finds the arbitrage leg the SHORT TERM IN EVERY YEAR by $50-150/kW-yr, with the RA leg second-order (and D33's, not a second storage mechanism). With the RA leg at its maximum AND the arbitrage leg at the real ISO-NE market's best year, li-ion 4 h is short in every year — a faithful merchant arbitrage-plus-FCA stack does not build 1.76 GW of New England batteries by 2030 on this cost basis. The screen's price object is a static re-price of the entering year's zonal duals that carries neither the tail nor the trough; the identified route is the GATED default-OFF entry_forward_expectation_signal (NEISO cell U), an entry-signal mechanism that moves every capacity screen rather than a storage one (rule 19), and its zero-cost precondition is entry_screen_diagnostics on the next NEISO solve. THE HORIZON'S SOLE ENTRY — 720 MW of 100-h iron_air in 2050 (evolution_2050.json; 0.6 tech-share cap x 1,200 MW NEISO annual cap; no second tech claims the remaining 480 MW) — falls after the anchor window and is a DATA-channel result: the RC-R demand-curve intake's re-timed exits tighten the 2049-2050 stack. It is NOT a D-3-rank result; D-3 is sign-preserving and chose among clearers, of which iron-air was the only one (D36 §1, §4). AEO carries ~1.0 GW more diurnal storage by 2030; the corridor number is context, never a target (rule 13). Source: D36 §7 (docs/handoffs/FINDING-capx-d36-storage-valuestack-2026-09-02.md), routed §8 item 1; re-authored by D38, 2026-09-02.

rows.model_basis: trajectory co2_mt (dispatch x per-generator emission rates)
rows.explanation: The 45Q + resolved-RGGI CCS retrofit wave, CORRECTLY RATED. The spec-§5.6 screen converts the CC fleet at its 3 GW/yr cap from 2028 (this bundle: 6,979.7 MW gas_cc_ccs beside 4,347.1 MW unabated gas_cc at 2030) under the 45Q window (ira_ccus_45q_last_year=2032) plus the resolved RGGI escalator ($26.05/t 2026 -> $132.16/t 2050, D23 §2; carbon_price field 0.0, program-resolved). AEO also carries RGGI at a far lower allowance path and retrofits nothing. Model CO2 at 2030 is now LOWER (-28.2 %) because the converted fleet emits at its CAPTURED rate: 21.286 TWh of the 33.925 TWh gas total is abated gas_cc_ccs. THIS ROW'S SIGN IS REVERSED FROM THE PRIOR TABLE (+60.6 % -> -25.0 %), and the reversal is not a model change: it is capx D77's repair of the CCS emission-rate seam (data/fleet/campd_bins.py::apply_plant_emission_rates_v2 re-booked a converted unit's UNCAPTURED host rate over its captured one in every forecast year), which the prior table's bundle predates. The renewable shortfall the prior explanation leaned on is unchanged and still present (generation:renewables row, -40.9 %); it is simply no longer large enough to outweigh a correctly-rated abated fleet. capx D96 (2026-09-25, owner ruling Q69) re-based this row onto the post-F1 bundle (eGRID-2024 heat rates): divergence -25.0 % -> -28.2 %, quoted figures refreshed; the mechanism is unchanged.

rows.model_basis: capacity_by_fuel_mw[coal]
gas_cc + gas_cc_ccs
rows.explanation: The self-limiting retrofit wave -- NEW EVIDENCE, not a restatement. On the repaired emission-rate seam (capx D77) a converted unit pays roughly one tenth of its host's carbon adder, which depresses BOTH the margin that would justify the next retrofit AND the margin that keeps the marginal unabated CC alive; D77 predicted exactly this self-limiting effect and named the 2029/2030 retrofit-set reshuffle as its signature. At 2040 the total CC fleet (gas_cc + gas_cc_ccs) is 10,142.5 MW -- 5,347.1 unabated + 4,795.4 abated -- against AEO's 12,779.7 MW of unabated CC held flat across the horizon. Ours-vs-theirs: AEO retrofits nothing and therefore never prices a retrofit against a retirement, so its CC fleet has no mechanism to shrink; the model's spec-§5.6 step-2/step-3 JOINT retrofit-or-retire screen does. The prior table had this row IN CORRIDOR at +2.8 % on a bundle carrying the defect. Stated as an OPEN root cause and not a closed one: whether the model's CC fleet SHOULD shrink this far is the question capx D90-R routed as "the CCS retrofit wave's size or economics", and this lane does not resolve it. capx D96 (2026-09-25, owner ruling Q69) re-based this row onto the post-F1 bundle (eGRID-2024 heat rates): divergence -20.2 % -> -20.6 %, quoted figures refreshed; the mechanism is unchanged.
